subject: biology
title: Reflex actions
key_idea: A **reflex action** is a fast, automatic response that protects the body. It follows a **reflex arc**: receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector. The pathway is short and does not involve the conscious part of the brain.

blocks.text: Some responses happen without thinking. This section covers what makes an action a reflex and gives examples.

items.meaning: An automatic, rapid response to a stimulus that does not involve the conscious part of the brain.
The pathway of neurones that carries the impulse in a reflex action.

items: A reflex is **fast** and **automatic**. It is involuntary and not under conscious control.
It does not involve thinking.
It **protects** the body from harm or danger.
Pulling a hand away from a hot or sharp object.
Blinking when an insect flies into the eye.
Releasing saliva when food enters the mouth.
Not a reflex: catching a dropped ruler. This is voluntary and uses the conscious part of the brain.
Reflexes are rapid, automatic and protective.
They happen without conscious thought.
A response that needs a decision is not a reflex.

blocks.text: A reflex arc uses three neurones in a fixed order. The example below is a hand touching a hot pan.

diagram.alt: A self-test: put the stages of a reflex arc in order, from the hot pan to the hand moving away.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of this reflex arc in order. A hand touches a hot pan.
steps: Receptor in the skin detects the heat (stimulus)
Impulse travels along the sensory neurone
First synapse: a chemical crosses the gap
Relay neurone in the spinal cord (CNS)
Second synapse: a chemical crosses the gap
Motor neurone carries the impulse to the muscle
Muscle (effector) contracts and the hand moves away

items: The **receptor** detects the stimulus and starts an electrical impulse.
The **sensory neurone** carries the impulse to the CNS.
The **relay neurone** in the spinal cord passes it on. The synapses are in the spinal cord or CNS.
The **motor neurone** carries the impulse to the **effector**, a muscle or gland.
At each synapse the impulse becomes a chemical that crosses the gap, then a new impulse.
Order: stimulus, receptor, sensory, relay, motor, effector, response.
Synapses join the neurones. A chemical crosses each gap.
The coordinator is the spinal cord (CNS).

blocks.text: The pathway is short and the conscious brain is bypassed. This makes the response quicker than a decision would be.

diagram.alt: A comparison of a reflex action and a voluntary action.
items: Reflex action
Voluntary action
Reflexes avoid (further) damage, such as a burn getting worse.
The response needs to be rapid.
Sending the impulse via the conscious brain would slow down the reaction time.
Myelin sheaths around neurones also speed up the impulses.
Fewer steps and no thinking mean a faster response.
A fast response limits harm.
Voluntary actions are slower because the brain decides.

checks.q: Give two features of a reflex action.
checks.a: Any two from: fast / rapid; automatic / involuntary (not under conscious control); protects from danger or harm; a response to a stimulus.

checks.q: Name the structures a nerve impulse passes through in a reflex arc, in order.
checks.a: Receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone (in the CNS), motor neurone, effector.

checks.q: Explain why it is important that pulling a hand away from a hot plate is a reflex.
checks.a: It avoids further damage. The reaction needs to be rapid. Involving the brain would slow the reaction.

mistakes.wrong: A reflex action is an action that is quick.
mistakes.right: Action and quick are ignored. Say it is a response or reaction, and that it is automatic, involuntary or not conscious.

mistakes.wrong: The receptor in the finger detects pain.
mistakes.right: Pain is ignored. Say the receptor in the skin detects the stimulus, such as heat or a temperature change.

mistakes.wrong: The synapses are in the brain.
mistakes.right: Brain is ignored. Say the synapses are in the spinal cord or CNS.

worked_example.question:
A woman's hand accidentally touches a hot object. The woman moves her hand away rapidly.

Describe how the woman's nervous system coordinates the reflex action.
answer_points: A receptor in the skin of the hand detects the stimulus (the temperature change).
Impulses pass from sensory to relay to motor neurones.
At a synapse between neurones, a chemical crosses the gap.
The synapses are in the spinal cord (CNS).
The effector is a muscle, and it contracts to pull the hand away.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each of six points. Say impulses, not messages, and say spinal cord or CNS rather than brain.

mistakes.wrong: A reflex arc protects the body.
mistakes.right: Link it to speed. It is an involuntary process that bypasses the brain, so there is a faster response and the body is protected from harm.

mistakes.wrong: Messages are sent from the brain to the muscles along a sensory neurone.
mistakes.right: Messages go as electrical impulses along a motor neurone to the effector.

mistakes.wrong: A reflex arc is a voluntary response to danger.
mistakes.right: It is involuntary (or subconscious), and it bypasses the brain or parts of the brain.

worked_example.question: Describe the structure and function of a reflex arc.
answer_points: A stimulus is detected by a receptor.
The receptor transfers the signal to the sensory neurone.
The sensory neurone transfers the signal to the CNS (brain, spinal cord or relay neurone).
The signal is transferred to a motor neurone, and a myelin sheath speeds up the electrical impulse.
The motor neurone transmits the signal to the effector, which produces the response.
Function: a rapid response, to protect the body from danger, which is involuntary and automatic.
worked_example.tip: This is marked in levels. For the top level, describe the whole structure in order and also state the function.

mistakes.wrong: The impulse goes along the sensory neurone to the brain, then to the muscle.
mistakes.right: Brain is ignored in a reflex. Say the impulse goes to the spinal cord or CNS.

mistakes.wrong: Receptors, motor neurone, sensory neurone, effector.
mistakes.right: The marks are only given when the points are in the correct sequence: receptor, sensory neurone, CNS, motor neurone, effector.

mistakes.wrong: A reflex is important because it is quick.
mistakes.right: Give the reasons: to avoid further damage, the reaction needs to be rapid, and the brain would slow down the reaction time.

worked_example.question:
A boy picks up a hot plate and quickly drops it. This is a reflex action.

Describe the sequence of events that happens in his nervous system during this reflex action.
answer_points: The stimulus is detected by receptors in the skin.
An impulse is sent along a sensory neurone.
The impulse goes to the spinal cord (CNS).
An impulse is sent along a motor neurone.
The impulse reaches the muscles (effectors) in the hand or arm.
worked_example.tip: The marks are only awarded when the events are in the correct sequence. Do not send the impulse via the brain.
